messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER — GPU pool dense-rtx reporting capacity saturation + driver error spike. Paging level: SEV2. queue_length=1200, p99_latency=12.4s, error_rate=18% :rotating_light:
ashley: seeing huge queued requests, autoscaler keeps hitting max_nodes. api error `scale rejected: quota_exceeded`
matt: confirmed, autoscaler attempted 3 scale ops in last 5m and stayed at 18 nodes (max_nodes=18)
devon: logs show recurrent CUDA Xid 31 and occasional OOMs on node gpu-rtx-07
lina: can we reroute non-critical routes to lower-cap models? That should buy us headroom
raj: on it — adding a temporary routing rule to downgrade embedding jobs and background batches to small-cluster (no SLA impact for critical customers)
ashley: pushing a quick policy: route label "batch=*" -> model: gpt-small-v2, weight=1.0; apply now
ops-bot: policy update accepted. affected routes: 4 services, est reduction queue ~350
ashley: autoscaler is still throttled by account quota. I've requested quota bump to cloud, but that won't be instant
matt: any sign of driver/kernel rollout that could correlate? We pushed kernel-driver-530 two days ago
devon: yes, kernel logs from gpu-rtx-07 show repeated entries: ```
[ERROR] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, PID 1219 (python), GPU has fallen off the bus
[WARN] oom_kill: invoked for process 1219 (llm_worker)
[INFO] nvidia-modedrv: failing health check, restarting driver
```
lina: that matches other nodes: 05 and 09 showing same pattern
ashley: immediate mitigation options?
devon: two quick ones: 1) cordon+drain the most symptomatic nodes and let the scheduler reallocate pods (risk: longer cold starts). 2) restart nvidia-driver on hosts (faster but might not stick if kernel mismatch)
raj: I can restart driver on 07 and 05 now, low risk window ~20s per node. Wants thumbs?
ashley: do it but one at a time. coord with autoscaler to avoid flapping. set node-nodrain label to avoid double-scheduling
raj: starting restart on gpu-rtx-07 -> sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver ; tail -n 200 /var/log/syslog for Xid entries
ops-bot: restart job queued (job id 8732)
raj: DONE on gpu-rtx-07. quick healthcheck: driver back, no Xid in last 30s, node marked Ready
ashley: queue dropped 180 in 2m, p99 down to 9.1s. still above normal though
matt: trying controlled drain on gpu-rtx-09 next, cordon then evict non-critical pods (batch/low-prio)
devon: note: autoscaler won't add nodes because account hit region GPU cap. If restart doesn't hold, we need two options: 1) emergency capacity increase via partner cloud account, 2) graceful degradation for some customers
ashley: opening a support ticket with cloud provider for an emergency quota increase (ticket #INC-84321). ETA unknown
cs-sarah: heads up — CSMs are getting customer reports about slow inference on a few large accounts. Can we get a brief customer impact note?
ashley: yes. draft: "We are experiencing degraded inference latency due to GPU node instability causing queueing. We have mitigations in place (driver restarts, routing lower-priority work to smaller models). Critical customer traffic is being prioritized. We will provide updates every 15 minutes." Anyone edit?
cs-sarah: add note: "Estimated impacted customers: <3 enterprise customers on us-east-1>. No data loss reported."
ashley: sent to CSMs.
devon: gpu-rtx-09 drain started. evictions hitting some pods that will cold-start. monitoring p99 for svc/streamer now
ashley: temp autoscale config: set aggressive_scale_down=false to avoid immediate collapse once nodes go back. Also toggled batching window to 50ms for low-priority routes (reduce token cost)
raj: after restart of 05 and 07, logs still show intermittent Xid 31 on 05. I'm going to try rolling back nvidia driver from 530 -> 525 on 05 as last resort
matt: coordinate rollback during low traffic window, but we need to do it now — traffic already degraded
raj: rolling back driver on gpu-rtx-05 (this will cause ephemeral pod restarts)
ops-bot: rollback job started (job id 8739)
raj: rollback complete on 05, kernel module reloaded, Xid traces cleared. node back to Ready
ashley: queue is now 210 total, p99 = 6.2s. error rate down to 4.3% :tada:
devon: still seeing two nodes with elevated memory pressure but within tolerable limits. Autoscaler still limited by max_nodes; quota request pending with cloud.
matt: mitigation status: driver restart/rollback = partial; routing downgrade = effective; autoscale quota = blocker for full recovery.
ashley: Customer impact: Severity=SEV2 (degraded performance for small set of customers). No token loss. Communication: CSMs notified, status page updated with note.
cs-sarah: CSMs pushed proactive messages to affected accounts, they're appreciative of proactive triage
ashley: next steps: 1) Follow up with cloud for quota bump (ticket INC-84321) 2) Run a 24h canary on driver 525 across a subset of nodes 3) Add autoscaler backoff to avoid thrash during driver churn 4) Create postmortem draft (assignments: devon -> driver logs & rollback timeline; matt -> autoscaler telemetry; lina -> routing rule audit; ashley -> customer comms & sev assessment)
devon: I'll own the driver timeline, collecting dmesg and kernel oops across all nodes, will attach logs to postmortem
matt: I'll gather autoscaler decisions and policy traces for the period 14:02–14:28 UTC
ashley: handing off to devon for next 30m oncall. devon: you're Hotofficer now. Please escalate if we hit repeat Xids after rollback.
devon: acknowledged. will monitor and update every 10m.
ashley: added retrospective action: increase regional gpu quota thresholds and add emergency capacity runbook.
ops-bot: incident thread archived to incidents channel with severity SEV2, incident id rwd-2026-04-28-17
ashley: thanks all. final note for handoff: current queue 195, p99 5.9s, 3 nodes were restarted/rolled back, autoscaler still constrained, cloud ticket open. devon now oncall.
ashley reacts with :thumbsup:
devon: will follow up with a short postmortem draft in ~2 hours and link to logs.
cs-sarah: sending customer follow-up now.
ops-bot: Scheduled follow-up reminder in 2 hours for postmortem draft.
